notes: Copy pass for the kpos-shell v2 integration. Grounded against ui-demos/kpos-shell/README.md (all sections), lore/bible.md, lore/ledger.md, content/customers.ts (full 12-customer roster), and content/story.ts for Rhea's shipped voice. This replaces this agent's prior proposal file (deep-balance-2026-07-28 cycle); that content is already integrated and is not resubmitted. Item types used are the two this brief specifies, 'inbox-subject' and 'ui-copy' (bespoke for this integration cycle, distinct from the general kp-contracts schema list), plus one 'ui-copy' item used to carry the INTRUSION-rename ruling request since no dedicated ruling-flag item type exists. Checked pipeline/copy/orders/: all 13 files are already status filled/done/cancelled, none open this cycle, so no teach-copy items are included; nothing owed there right now. No scene, journal, or dayline items included either: this is a pure UI-copy integration pass and I found no gap in the reveal schedule that demands a new story beat, so runOpenerScene/runEndScene/JOURNAL_ENTRIES/DAY_LINES are untouched. No art orders filed: nothing in this cycle's narrative-director scope is a new diegetic story moment (the customer-figure-likeness and BENCH FEED diegetic-claim questions the brief's Gates section raises belong to ux-agent/art-lead, who commissioned that art; I'm not ordering new art against my own scope this cycle). Inbox subjects: one item per customerId (tier field omitted throughout) rather than one per customer-tier pair. A customer's standing complaint reads the same regardless of which difficulty tier serves up that day's ticket (customers.ts does not vary quotes/winLine/lossLine by tier either), so one Rhea line already covers every tier a customer appears at; noted here explicitly as a deliberate choice, not an oversight, in case a future pass wants tier-escalating subjects for recurring customers like Aldous Wick (T1-3) or Ines Calloway (T3-4). Subject format bakes in the brief's own illustrative example ('RE: <device>') as literal leading text, not presentational chrome, since that is the safer default: trivial for the Orchestrator to strip a leading 'RE: ' if the ux-agent spec wants to render it as chrome instead, much harder to retrofit if baked-in text turns out to be wanted. Every subject line is new Rhea-voiced copy, not adopted from the INBOX study's demo-mock subjects (those paraphrase the CUSTOMER's complaint in the customer's own register; the brief is explicit that shipped subjects must read as RHEA routing the order, a different speaker and a different job), built from her established voice (dry, protective, deflects into logistics, per lore/bible.md and the day-open lines in story.ts such as 'The Kestrel courier drone is back. Same customer, new complaint.' and 'The Ledgerstone pawn vault sent someone over again. Good, they pay on time.').

items.surface: DIVE.EXE (every duel surface: board port tag, turn pair, telemetry heading, entry-node tag, console prose)
items.key: LOREMASTER RULING REQUESTED: opponent identity tag, SIG-0 to INTRUSION
items.notes: Per the brief's explicit instruction, presenting this as an item for the Loremaster to rule on rather than deciding it myself. Current state: the shipped duel board labels the opposing port SIG-0 (a cold signal id, duel-board.tsx:186); the shipped threat-banner prose already uses 'INTRUSION' as a common noun in running text ('INTRUSION n ROTATIONS FROM THE CORE', duel.tsx:631) but not as the opponent's on-screen identity tag. The kpos-shell study renames every identity-bearing surface to INTRUSION uniformly: board port tag, the YOU|INTRUSION turn-pair toggle, the telemetry rail's h3 heading, and the entry-node tag. My assessment, offered for the ruling, not as a decision: this reads as safe. 'Intrusion' is already the world's own generic term for any AI signal occupying a device that is not yours (lore/bible.md: 'Intrusions are epidemic... Every shop ticket is an intrusion job.'), so labeling the opposing port INTRUSION is the interface using the same technical classification it already uses everywhere else, not naming or personifying an individual character the way Patch is named. It does not touch Patch, grant a pronoun beyond what already exists, or state a truth claim about any specific opponent's nature; it reads as 'what kind of signal is this' the same for Juno Vex's ghost as for anything else DIVE.EXE ever renders. The one case worth the Loremaster's direct eye: back-room/tutorial dives (runs 1 to 12, pre-finale) also route through DIVE.EXE per the brief's integration architecture ('DIVE.EXE replaces the duel presentation wholesale... INTRUSION naming... Finale and tutorial get dressed variants'), meaning the sealed-room opponent, eventually revealed as Patch, would also read INTRUSION on screen throughout. I read this as consistent with the erosion being played honest (ledger: Rhea's virus theory 'was always a reasonable in-world inference,' and the shop's own detection apparatus genuinely cannot yet tell Patch from any other occupant, which is exactly why her guess was reasonable) rather than the interface asserting a claim the story later contradicts; the label is Diagnostic ('this port holds an intrusion-class signal'), not biographical. If the finale's 'dressed variant' of DIVE.EXE is meant to relabel the opponent once revealed, that relabeling is not specified anywhere I could find and should be decided alongside this ruling. Flagging for the record, not asking to gate the whole rename on it: SIG-0 to INTRUSION at duel-board.tsx:186 is the one line the Orchestrator must also change if this rules in favor, since the README notes it 'does not carry over' on its own.

items.key: the whole BUS.LOG vocabulary: boot lines, round dividers, player actions, machine and world events
items.notes: All 26 lines adopt verbatim from dive.ts; this is the full vocabulary, not just the five examples the README's inventory paragraph quotes as representative. Deliberately all lowercase (actor prefix YOU>/INT>/SYS> already carries the caps distinction per the study's own color/weight convention), terminal and clipped, no dashes throughout; reads as a real bus tap, not a narrator. {addr} is the engine's existing hex bus address format (0x plus two uppercase hex digits, e.g. 0x2A), {n} and mode labels are already-live engine values, none of this needs new invention beyond confirming the words. Flagging one register question for the Orchestrator/ux-agent rather than deciding it: dive-report.html's demo REPAIR.LOG dive-log rail uses hand-authored ALL CAPS per-scenario flavor lines ('R01 LINK UP. HEXLIGHT BOOTS TO ATTRACT MODE'), a different case register than this lowercase BUS.LOG. Per the brief's own integration architecture, REPAIR.LOG's dive log is meant to list 'the actual duel events of the finished dive', i.e. a replay of this exact BUS.LOG stream with round-number prefixes, not a separately authored case-log register; I recommend REPAIR.LOG inherit this lowercase vocabulary unchanged (just prefixed with its round number) so a replay reads as literally the same words the player saw live, rather than a re-cased rewrite. If a distinct all-caps 'closed case' register is wanted for REPAIR.LOG specifically, that is a presentation call for ux-agent, not mine, and I can supply an all-caps transposition on request.

Adopt verbatim from dive.ts (`ON THE BENCH // ${cust.device.toUpperCase()}`). {DEVICE} is the customer's existing customers.ts device string, uppercased. The diegetic claim this tag makes (the OS shows what the bench is physically tapped into) is named in the brief's Gates section for the Loremaster; that is a diegetic-claim ruling parallel to the BENCH FEED one, not a wording question, so I'm not re-litigating it here, only confirming the tag text.

items.notes: heroWinGridlock/heroWinCore/heroLossSevered/heroLossCore/viewBoardButton are already shipped verbatim in the current duel.tsx result overlay; confirming for the record. newDiveButton replaces the shipped 'CONTINUE' button: the standalone study reboots the same scenario with a fresh seed, but read as a control label it also works cleanly as 'this ticket is done, open the next dive', which is the actual production meaning once DIVE.EXE closes back to INBOX/REPAIR.LOG. Recommending NEW DIVE over CONTINUE going forward since 'continue' implied invisible progression inside one screen, and the new windowed-desktop metaphor wants an explicit, diegetic control label like every other action in this redesign; flagging that the exact handoff behavior behind the button (does it literally start a fresh dive, or dismiss back to REPAIR.LOG/INBOX) is an Orchestrator integration decision, not a copy one. The five bill rows are genuinely new: the shipped duel.tsx result overlay currently states strain as one inline sentence ('Neural Strain zeroes. The run is over.'; 'Messy work. Neural Strain -{chip}.') with no itemized breakdown; the study's dv-result-bill splits this into a labeled datarow list. Proposing these five labels for the gate: ROUNDS/ROTATIONS/TRAPS FIRED ON YOU/STRAIN CHIP as bare ALL CAPS datarow labels (matching the .kp-datarow-plain convention ux-agent's kpos-design-language already specifies elsewhere in this cycle), and billNeuralStrainLossValue as the value shown in the NEURAL STRAIN row on a loss, replacing the old inline sentence with a label plus this short value so the row reads as a receipt line, not a sentence fragment.
